questions.question: Explain the term value chain using the example of a T-shirt (cotton R10, factory sells to shop for R60, shop sells for R120), showing the value added at each stage.
questions.expected_answer: A value chain is the sequence of stages from raw material to final consumer, each adding value. Primary (cotton farmer): R10. Secondary (factory): 60 - 10 = R50. Tertiary (shop): 120 - 60 = R60. Total value added = 10 + 50 + 60 = R120 = final price.

questions.question: Give one way each sector depends on each of the other two.
questions.expected_answer: Primary depends on secondary for machinery, fertiliser, fuel and electricity, and on tertiary for transport, finance, insurance and selling/exporting. Secondary depends on primary for raw materials (wheat, iron ore, cotton) and on tertiary for transport, retail, finance and skilled workers. Tertiary depends on primary and secondary for the goods it sells, transports and uses (food, vehicles, fuel, buildings, electricity).

questions.question: Describe the ripple effects of a mine closure on all three sectors.
questions.expected_answer: Primary: mine workers lose jobs and output falls. Secondary: suppliers of equipment, explosives and boots lose a customer and cut jobs. Tertiary: local shops, taxis, salons and guest houses lose customers; banks face unpaid loans; municipal revenue falls; families receiving remittances lose income.
